title: Captions only when you ask for them
goal: User 2026-09-28: 'I do not want closed captions generated proactively, I'd prefer to have a way to add closed captions for a video on demand.' This reverses the earlier ask for captions to extract themselves on open (EditorState.swift calls writeCaptionsByThemselves() when a recording opens; the Captions panel has an Auto switch). The user's latest word wins. Ask: how does Premiere, CapCut or Descript offer this: one clear Generate Captions action.
notes: Filed from the intake window. Supersedes the auto-on-open part of captions-write-themselves-from-the-speech (done).
acceptance: Opening a recording never starts transcription: writeCaptionsByThemselves and the Auto switch are removed (and any setting that turned it on), with no background speech work at all until asked

Captions are added on demand from: right-click a clip or audio segment > Add Captions; the timeline's + (add track) menu > Captions; and the Edit or Video menu > Add Captions (Premiere's Transcribe); the result lands as the Captions layer and track
While transcribing, a small progress indicator sits on the new captions track and the editor stays fully usable; Cancel stops it
The Captions panel section, with no captions yet, shows one Add Captions button and nothing else
Existing documents that already have captions keep them
The captions tasks still open (captions-are-one-layer..., how-the-words-show..., fix-a-caption-one-word...) are updated to say captions are made on demand
Walk at Next defaults: open a recording with speech, wait 10 s, confirm no transcription ran and no captions track exists; add captions from the clip's right-click; photograph both states
